editorial.headline: A National Opening, a Bali PMA Stop
editorial.standfirst: This activity embraces specialist sports-goods retail nationwide, yet foreign investors cannot register it for PMA in Bali under the island-wide moratorium.
editorial.body:
KBLI 47620 is the retail activity for sports equipment and supplies, but its practical terrain is wider than a rack of balls or racquets. The stated scope includes fishing equipment; hunting weapons and ammunition; camping goods; boats; and bicycles, including electric bicycles, unicycles, hoverboards, scooters and Segways. It also takes in specialist sports footwear—football boots, ice skates and ski boots—and specialist sports apparel for skiing, martial arts and ballet. Parachutes, tents and sleeping bags sit within the same retail perimeter. Ordinary, non-specialised sports footwear, including tennis, basketball, gym and training shoes, is expressly outside it.

The relevant question for a founder is therefore whether the proposed assortment belongs to this specialised retail field, not whether it merely has a sporting association. The record admits the activity at every stated business scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. That range matters because the activity is framed as retail trade across a broad set of named goods and formats, from mobility equipment to outdoor and specialist-performance articles. The classification detail stays focused on those specified retail lines.

At the national level, the PMA position is clear. The status is TERBUKA and the maximum foreign ownership stated for this activity is 100%. In plain terms, the national record treats it as open to foreign investment up to a full foreign stake. That national opening is sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. It should be read as the national position for this activity rather than as an answer to where it may be registered within Indonesia.

That distinction decides the Bali outcome. Bali marks the activity as blocked by risk class, and the record says that, at the Besar scale, its OSS risk is Rendah or Menengah-Rendah across every scope. Those ratings place the activity inside Bali’s island-wide, permanent moratorium on PMA registration for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI. The result is direct: a foreigner cannot register this activity for PMA in Bali today. The national 100% ceiling remains the national ceiling; it does not override the Bali moratorium. For a plan centred on Bali, that is the operative fact—not a marginal qualification to an otherwise open national classification.
